March 17, 34.

Dear Mr. Sarly,

I forward herewith for your information tabulated
statement relating to the arrest by the Municipal Police
of a communist named Iung Kyi Hau (应钦浩) alias Iung
Pao Kong (危宝康) at 7.40 p.m. March 5, 1934 on North
Honan Road.

The accused was charged on remand before the Second
Branch of the Kiangsu High Court on March 14, 1934 when
he was ordered to be handed over to the Chinese authorities.

Yours sincerely,

HR

Subject (in full) Arrest of a communist suspect named Iung Kyi Hau (應欽浩)
outside the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building on North Honan Road.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [签名]

With reference to the endorsement of the Deputy
Commissioner, Special Branch, on the attached file dated
March 5, 1934, relating to the arrest of a communist suspect
named Iung Kyi Hau (應欽浩) alias Iung Pao Kong (應宝康) at
7.30 p.m. March 5, 1934, I have to report the following :-
The Chung Hwa (中華) Evening News Printing Works,
462 North Honan Road, which was formerly used as an editorial
and printing office for the publication of an evening paper
known as the Chung Hwa Evening News, has been in existence
since May 1929 and is the property of one Feng Sz Shih (馮梓石),
nephew of a well-known Chinese lawyer Feng Ping Nan (馮炳南).
The publication of this paper ceased in May 1933 owing to bad
business following which a mosquito paper known as the "New
World Journal" (新世界报) was printed for a period of three months.
The Chung Hwa Evening News Printing Works, although without any
business, still retains four employees on the premises as the
management has not yet reached any decision regarding the course
of work to be undertaken. As far as can be ascertained, this
printing shop entertains no political leanings.
As regards the Kwang Ming (光明) Print Works (File D-585)
which was formerly located at No.89 Park Road, the ex-manager,
Yui Zien Sung (俞先松), was on September 9, 1925, arraigned
before the defunct Mixed Court to answer a summons which had
been issued at the request of the Shanghai Municipal Police
following the discovery of a number of booklets of an
inflammatory nature in his shop. On September 30, 1925, he was
convicted and sentenced as follows:-
"Fined $100 and warned that if he repeats the offence
he will be expelled."

主题（全称） 在河南北路中国商会大楼外逮捕一名名为應欽浩（Iung Kyi Hau，又名應宝康 Iung Pao Kong）的共产党嫌疑犯。

由督察顾保华（Kuh Pao-hwa）制作。经由 [签名] 转呈

关于特别分部副总监在附件档案（日期为1934年3月5日）上的批示，该档案涉及1934年3月5日晚7时30分逮捕一名名为應欽浩（Iung Kyi Hau，又名應宝康 Iung Pao Kong）的共产党嫌疑犯一事，现报告如下：
中华（Chung Hwa）晚报印刷厂，位于河南北路462号，此前用作编辑和印刷办公室，出版一份名为《中华晚报》的晚报，该厂自1929年5月成立以来一直存在，归冯梓石（Feng Sz Shih）所有，他是著名中国律师冯炳南（Feng Ping Nan）的侄子。由于生意不佳，该报于1933年5月停刊，随后印刷了一份名为《新世界报》的小报，为期三个月。中华晚报印刷厂虽然没有任何业务，但仍保留四名员工在场，因为管理层尚未就下一步的工作方向做出任何决定。据查，这家印刷店没有任何政治倾向。
至于光明（Kwang Ming）印刷厂（档案 D-585），该厂以前位于公园路89号，前经理俞先松（Yui Zien Sung）于1925年9月9日被传讯至已撤销的混合法庭，回应应上海公共租界工部局警务处之请求发出的传票，原因是其店内发现数本煽动性小册子。1925年9月30日，他被定罪并判处如下刑罚：
“罚款100元，并警告若再犯将被驱逐。”

The aforementioned premises were also visited on September
4, 1929, by the Municipal Police on the authority of a search
warrant issued at the instance of the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison
Commissioner's Headquarters. Nothing, however, of an incriminating
nature was found.
On March 3, 1930, the address in question was again visited
by the Municipal Police in search of seditious publications
but without success.
According to information at hand, the Kwang Ming Printing
Shop, as shown in preceding paragraphs, was formerly connected
with anti-government activities, but ceased business operations
in the summer of 1932 owing to financial difficulties and is no
longer in existence.
The accused in this case was actually enticed from the
Chung Hwa Evening News Printing Works by an informer of the
Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety named Lau Ling (差林), with
whom, according to information furnished by the Chinese Authorities,
a rendezvous had been made for that evening (March 5, 1934)
inside the library of the Chamber of Commerce Building on North
Honan Road. Sung Kwei Tsung (孙闺忠), the apprentice, only
delivered the verbal message that a friend of the accused desired
to meet him outside the shop, so it will be seen that he (the
apprentice) did so without any malicious intent.
Lau Ling, the P.S.B. informer, is a reformed communist
and was formerly working together with the accused in the
Publication Section of the Shanghai Central District Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party. Apart from this, the Chinese
Authorities do not possess any other material evidence to support
their claim.

上述处所也曾于1929年9月4日由市政警察凭淞沪警备司令部总部签发的搜查令进行搜查。然而，未发现任何罪证。
1930年3月3日，市政警察再次前往该地址搜寻颠覆性出版物，但未成功。
根据手头掌握的信息，如前几段所述，光明印刷厂以前与反政府活动有关，但因财务困难于1932年夏季停止营业，现已不复存在。
本案被告实际上是被上海市公安局一名名为差林（Lau Ling）的线人从中华晚报印刷厂诱出的，据中国当局提供的信息，双方约定当晚（1934年3月5日）在河南北路商会大楼的图书馆内会面。学徒孙闺忠（Sung Kwei Tsung）仅口头传达消息说被告的一位朋友想在店外见他，由此可见他（学徒）这样做并无恶意。
劳林（Lau Ling，即差林），上海市公安局线人，是一名改过自新的共产党员，以前与被告一起在中国共产党上海中央区委员会出版科工作。除此之外，中国当局没有任何其他物证来支持他们的主张。

Ningpo                                          D/SZ Sansom (Sp. Br.)
W/Hongkew Stn      March 5, 1934                Clerk Kao Yen-keng
                                                       (Sp. Br.)

    My name is Ying Chingchao, age 25, native of Ningpo,
single, a typesetter by profession, employed and residing
in the Chung Hwa Evening News Printing Works, 462 North
Soochow Road.
    I studied in a private school at Shaoshing between
the ages of 7 and 12.    I was then without work
until I was 17 years old, when I came to Shanghai and
obtained employment at Kwang Ming (光明) Printing
Shop on Park Road, completing my apprenticeship there
at the age of 20.    Subsequent to that I worked in
numerous printing shops in the Settlement until the
beginning of 1933.    I then became unemployed and
resided at both Ningpo and Shanghai, living chiefly on
the support of one of my brother's named Ying Ping'an
(應聘安), who resides at 15 Yoch Hwa Faung (月華坊),
Kinchow Road off Ward Road.    On December 25, 1933,
I obtained employment in the Chung Hwa Evening News
Printing Works, 462 North Soochow Road, remaining there
up to the present time.
    At about 7 p.m. today, March 5, 1934, whilst in
the printing works, an apprentice named Sung Kwangtsong
(宋光忠) informed me that friends were waiting for
me at North Honan and North Soochow Roads corner.    I
then walked around the corner to the main gate of the
3rd District Kuomintang Branch (Temple of the Queen of
Heaven) and was seized by four persons and hustled into
the Kuomintang Branch Headquarters from off the

    我叫应钦浩，25岁，宁波人，
未婚，职业为排字工人，受雇并居住于
苏州河北路 462 号中华晚报印刷所。
    我7至12岁时在绍兴的一所私塾读书。此后
一直失业，直到17岁那年来到上海，在
公园路的光明印刷店找到工作，并在该处
学徒期满，时年20岁。此后直至
1933年初，我在租界内的多家印刷店工作。
随后我失业，往返居住于宁波和上海两地，主要
依靠住在华德路近荆州路月华坊15号的
兄长应平安 (Ying Ping'an) 接济生活。1933年12月25日，
我在苏州河北路 462 号中华晚报印刷所找到工作，
并一直工作至今。
    今日，即1934年3月5日晚7时许，我正在
印刷所内，一名叫宋光忠 (Sung Kwangtsong) 的学徒
告知我，有朋友在河南路与苏州北路转角处
等我。于是我走到转角处，来到第三区国民党

In the courtyard of the Kuomintang Branch Headquarters,
I was slapped on the face and asked whether I had convened
any meeting. Five minutes later I was hustled off
the premises and was on the point of being placed in a
taxi when I hailed a passing □□□□ who brought me
to this station together with two of the men who seized
me. They accused me in the presence of the □□□□
of being a communist.

I am not interested in political affairs. An
accountant of the printing works, named Yu Soong-sung
(俞松盛), whom I have known for many years, can prove
that I seldom leave the place of my employment. He
can also vouch for my character and antecedents.

(Signed) Xing Qinghao.
